title: Sardar Patel and the Nizam: Operation Polo (1948)
culture_region: India / Greece / USA / South Africa / World
summary: 'Hyderabad is an ulcer in the belly of India; it must be surgically removed immediately', declared Patel, ensuring southern India's territorial integrity in four days.
keywords: Sardar Patel and the Nizam: Operation Polo (1948)
full_text:
In 1948, the Nizam of Hyderabad, Mir Osman Ali Khan—reputed to be the wealthiest man on earth—refused to accede to the Indian Union, harboring fantasies of an independent theocratic state aligned with Pakistan.

His fanatical Razakar militia under Qasim Razvi terrorized neighboring districts and oppressed the majority population.

While Prime Minister Nehru hesitated, fearing international diplomatic fallout, Home Minister Sardar Patel was adamantly resolute:
"Jawaharlal! You attend to foreign relations; leave Hyderabad to me!
Hyderabad is not on our outer frontier; it sits right in the belly of India!
Can a human body survive with a festering cancerous ulcer in its stomach?
The time for diplomatic telegrams is over; surgery is mandatory!"

On September 13, 1948, Patel ordered **Operation Polo**.

Under Major General J. N. Chaudhuri, Indian armored columns crossed into Hyderabad. Within one hundred hours—just four days—the Razakar forces collapsed, and the Nizam surrendered unconditionally.

On September 18, the humbled Nizam received Sardar Patel at the airport with folded hands.

Patel greeted him with serene composure:
"Nizam Sahib, fear not. You shall live in peace and honor as a citizen of the Indian Republic. But remember always: no individual and no ruler is greater than the sovereign unity of the Indian nation!"

Patel's decisive action preserved the peace and security of peninsular India forever.
moral: Timely and decisive action in defense of national integrity prevents decades of internal conflict and suffering.
